title: Audit temporal-position robustness of original VERA on CPU
body:
## Result
Completed a CPU-only audit of original VERA's final position weighting on all 290 UCF videos. Holding pre-position scores and labels paired, original weighting varies from 86.607% to 82.879% AUC across five fixed shifts. Removing it gives 85.600% at every shift: a 2.721 pp worst-position benefit, paired 95% CI [1.307, 4.371], with a 1.007 pp unshifted AUC cost.

**The predeclared practical gate fails:** worst-position benefit is below 3 pp. All four retrieval/endpoint settings fail that same requirement (benefit 2.699–2.758 pp). Thresholds were not changed, and no GPU/XD follow-up was launched. Removing weighting is already a published ablation; this audit does not establish algorithm novelty or end-to-end edited-video robustness.

## Reproduction and verification
- Protocol `819ba57` preceded feature download. Verified-asset/implementation freeze `3da8543` preceded performance measurements.
- Downloaded the 309,807,835-byte author feature release directly after the Drive connector's size-limit rejection. All 290 feature/score IDs, dimensions, row alignment, CRCs, finite values and nonzero norms passed; a previously verified feature checksum matches.
- Independent replay matches all 1,111,808 upstream scores bitwise and all labels exactly. Primary follows released-code 15% retrieval. Predeclared 10% sensitivity reproduces 86.548% AUC, rounding to the paper's 86.55%.
- Preserved a pre-performance relative-output-path launch failure and its invocation correction (`bc7e03f`). Preserved the failed replay and froze exact-upstream short-video convolution truncation (`3cce2c8`). No scientific criteria changed.
- Four cohorts, each with 1,000 paired whole-video bootstrap replicates. Five annotation endpoint discrepancies handled exactly as upstream, plus an exclusion sensitivity. Cached AUC agrees with explicit duplicated-video sklearn tests, including ties and constant scores. All 580 extracted inputs rehashed unchanged.
- Successful replay: 22.257 s; statistics: 206.368 s; local CPU, four BLAS threads. Zero model/GPU calls. External raw vectors and data are hashed; no blobs are committed.

## Report
Compiled `.tex` report with measured tables, two scientific figures, novelty limits, both corrections and the stopping decision. Full metrics, bootstrap samples and per-video/category diagnostics are included. PR11 records remain unchanged. No merge.

## Additive human-requested reassessment
The original frozen gate remains **FAIL**. The positive 2.721 pp effect with CI [1.307,4.371] is nevertheless measurable and merits considering a separately preregistered, bounded CPU-only XD confirmation. The unchanged original-order cost (1.007 AUC pp; 4.027 AP pp) prevents a uniform-improvement claim.

New primary-source checks (arXiv 2608.21854v1 and 2608.11985v2) narrow broad metric-audit novelty; VERA/CoReVAD already ablate weight removal. No algorithm novelty or priority is claimed. Additive `reassessment.tex` includes chronology, full tradeoffs, literature limits and a recommendation; the original report and all frozen performance results remain unchanged. The standalone researcher copy compiled successfully.

A reproducible metadata-only checker verifies all 800 released XD score/test IDs, ZIP CRCs, anchor grids/end lengths, AP binary labels and trimmed label lengths. Feature contents are not downloaded/verified; **no XD performance experiment or GPU call** occurred. The released XD AUC script applies position weighting, but the released AP script does not and uses different rounding/trimming and trapezoidal PR area. No claim that removal improves official XD AP is justified. Any future confirmation requires a separate protocol before performance and must preserve the original failed UCF gate.

## Summary by Sourcery

Audit VERA’s final temporal position weighting on UCF, document a measurable but sub-threshold robustness benefit, and preserve the decision not to launch automatic GPU or XD performance follow-up.

New Features:
- Add a reproducible CPU-only audit of VERA’s temporal position weighting across all 290 UCF videos, including fixed-shift counterfactuals, paired bootstrap analysis, and sensitivity cohorts.
- Add metadata-only XD asset feasibility checks without downloading features or running performance experiments.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct replay invocation paths and short-video convolution handling while preserving the frozen upstream behavior and scientific criteria.

Enhancements:
- Validate released UCF assets and independently reproduce all upstream scores and labels before evaluating counterfactuals.
- Document the measured robustness tradeoff, reproducibility evidence, statistical diagnostics, stopping decision, and limits on novelty and end-to-end interpretation.
- Add additive reassessment materials recommending a separately preregistered XD confirmation while retaining the original failed practical gate.

Documentation:
- Add protocols, reproduction instructions, reports, reassessment, audit trail, and provenance records for the CPU-only study.

Tests:
- Add metric correctness checks against explicit duplicated-video sklearn calculations, including ties, constant scores, shifts, labels, and gate behavior.

Chores:
- Add hashed evidence, bootstrap outputs, diagnostics, generated figures, and tables for the completed audit.

title: Evaluate frozen VERA abstention and selective explanations
body:
## Result
Training-free VERA prompt changes did not demonstrate better detection or useful selective explanations. In the complete 72-call comparison, both modified prompts retained 5 of 12 original alerts and made identical decisions on all 24 inputs. No model weights or guiding questions were trained.

## Experiments and documented repair
- First 48-call original/ternary proxy: insufficient outputs on 1/12 annotation-included and 5/12 gap views; retained 6/7 original annotated-view alerts. These are response counts, not accuracy.
- Three-condition protocol, runner and metrics frozen at `7778d09` before 72 calls. Original labels and raw text repeated exactly on all 24 inputs. Modified explanations copied literal template examples or emitted empty observations. Original metrics remain preserved; a separate content audit documents the defect.
- Repair frozen at `f355121` before inference: removed example values and required actual observations. It stopped after six calls when a response omitted its final Output label. Partial records, log and traceback are preserved without retry or a fabricated completion record.
- Actual consumption: 126 of 192 allowed calls. Ada 5 only, now released. No A16s, Adas 6/7 or separate firearm jobs were touched.

## Validation and reproducibility
Preserved raw prompts/responses, input/dependency provenance, completed and partial records, frozen reference hashes, original analysis, post-run audit, scientific figure and all 24 paired decisions. All 24 tensor checks passed. Eight complete-run and seven partial-run transfer hashes matched. Frozen protocols, runners and analysis remain unchanged; parser checks passed. The updated `.tex` report compiled successfully and explains VERA's shared-checkpoint learner/optimizer roles.

## Research decision
No established novelty: primary-source review found direct overlap with GroundedVQA, TRACE, refusal/readiness and anomaly-specific visual verification. Partial UCA references, lexical overlap and valid citations cannot establish claim correctness or reduced hallucinations. No learned extension or further GPU compute is justified in this prompt direction. Reopening requires a differentiated mechanism and stronger existing evidence-linked evaluation; new human annotation is not inherently necessary.

## Summary by Sourcery

Evaluate training-free VERA abstention and selective explanations, document the implementation failure and inconclusive results, and stop further work without stronger evidence or a differentiated mechanism.

New Features:
- Add reproducible protocols and tooling for metadata feasibility audits, blinded annotation calibration, abstention proxies, and selective-explanation comparisons.
- Add scoped reporting and evidence artifacts documenting training-free VERA abstention and explanation experiments.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct the selective-explanation output-template defect by removing placeholder examples and requiring concrete observations.
- Preserve and explicitly audit incomplete runs and malformed outputs instead of retrying or fabricating records.

Enhancements:
- Document experiment outcomes, limitations, novelty review, stopping criteria, and the decision not to pursue further GPU experiments in this prompt direction.
- Add deterministic input construction, provenance tracking, tensor/hash verification, strict parsing, content audits, and reproducible figures and tables.

Documentation:
- Add protocols, rubrics, reproduction guidance, novelty assessments, and a compiled research report covering the experiments and their limitations.

Tests:
- Add contract checks for binary outputs, explanation schemas, citations, and invalid response handling.

Chores:
- Preserve raw experiment records, partial-run artifacts, reference hashes, and compute accounting for reproducibility.

title: Assess original VERA evidence-feedback novelty and pilot data readiness
body:
## Research decision
Broad evidence-feedback prompt learning substantially overlaps with existing frozen-VLM anomaly work. This PR records the source review and data audit, then narrows the next investigation to whether temporal feedback distinguishes order effects from order-invariant controls. No novelty or model-performance improvement is claimed.

## New analytical result
LRPO Section 3.4 Eq.5 with Appendix C parameters gives positive temporal reward when ordered/shuffled accuracy rewards are equal (0.8/0.8 gives 0.117333), assuming a correct ordered output. This is a synthetic equation diagnostic, not a reproduction of author code or evidence against benchmark results. An additional strict outperformance gate would remove the counterexamples. Script, JSON, figure and report disclose this limitation.

Instance-Aligned Captions uses manual roles/boxes plus model-generated masks/captions; it is not wholly human-verified claim truth. UCF appears in its dataset table; XD does not. Annotation download access remains unestablished.

## Reproducibility and validation
- Exact-ID split audit: UCF 1449/161/290; XD 3559/395/800, disjoint IDs; source hashes recorded. No claim of scene independence.
- `python studies/vera_evidence/code/audit_temporal_reward.py`: five analytical assertions passed; JSON and scientific figures generated.
- `git diff --check` passed; LaTeX report compiled successfully with desktop compiler; figure visually inspected.
- No new GPU inference, no changes to frozen experiment03B records, no interference with other jobs.
- Next: check author implementation and prior order-null diagnostics, then freeze a small original-VERA exploratory protocol before allocation. Previously consulted UCF test videos cannot be called untouched confirmation or used to select learned prompts.

Report source: `studies/vera_evidence/feasibility_report.tex`. Base is the completed repair branch so this PR contains only the new research assessment.

## Completed original-VERA pilot
Protocol committed before inference (36c097d, repeat stop1eb2179). Eight hash-selected, source-unique exploratory UCF windows, 40 calls: exact identical-repeat agreement8/8; no reversal/shuffle decision changes (0/8 each), although text changed6/8 and5/8. Repeated-single-frame decisions changed2/8; that control also removes information. Zero parse failures/cap hits; processed tensor mappings verified. Raw responses, provenance, completion, SHA transfer checks, analyzer and plotting code included.89.54s process time on oneAda5 (~.025 GPU-hours); GPU released; original dependencies unchanged.

Updated .tex compiled successfully and plot visually inspected. No scale-up: first determine whether text variations are incompatible evidence claims; no novelty/faithfulness/improvement conclusion from this pilot. Existing03B records remain unchanged.

## Text review and scoped stop
All16 reversed/shuffled pairs reviewed with raw-response hashes (5 exactmatches). Descriptions differ substantively in some cases, but text alone does not prove mutually exclusive events or hallucination. This is explicitly a post-hoc Codex text-only review, without source-frame verification or human annotation. Stop temporal-pilot expansion; no more GPU calls from this finding. Evidence-question learning still requires independent support labels and a distinct mechanism. Report recompiled successfully. No original results modified.

## Accessible external annotations: UCA
Verified original authors' upstream commit e478cb5b2277c6b7cf6a1dc4691021592003e216; downloaded metadata, not videos. Audit script and six hashes included.1854 videos/23542 timed captions; valid interval structure and internally disjoint UCA splits. Crucially, UCA train overlaps VERA test by214videos. Default UCA training must NOT be used for VERA learning; joint training intersection863requires further source checks. External captions offer a conditional route, but stronger supervision must be disclosed and missing captions cannot label claims false. Updated report includes cross-split table and compiles. No additional GPU compute.

UCA annotation methodology verified from original paper: trained human annotation plus separate review. VANGUARD already uses UCA-aligned reasoning and grounding; frozen-question feedback novelty remains unresolved. Retained a deterministic ID-only candidate manifest and rejected it before inference because validation has10normal+2burglary videos. Next design must preserve VERA boundaries while using annotations across UCA's differing splits and explicitly ensure category coverage. No new GPU use; report recompiled.

## Final decision: no-go under current evidence
See RESEARCH_DECISION.md. Stop additional GPU runs, downloads and prompt optimization for this proposal. Available UCA references do not validate arbitrary generated claims; existing methods substantially overlap, and no precise differentiated mechanism has emerged. Data access is not the blocker:156 originalVERA validation IDs have UCA references across all categories. Reopening needs independent supported/contradicted/unknown labels with source evidence and matched-supervision/call controls. This is a bounded resource decision, not proof future novelty is impossible. All records preserved, final report compiled; total new compute~.025GPUh, no A16. No merge.

## Summary by Sourcery

Assess the novelty and readiness of evidence-feedback learning for VERA, preserve reproducible pilot findings, and stop further work on the proposal until independent claim-support labels and a differentiated mechanism are available.

New Features:
- Add a reproducible feasibility assessment of evidence-feedback question learning for frozen VERA anomaly detection, including literature, dataset, annotation, and split audits.
- Add an exploratory temporal-order pilot and supporting artifacts to evaluate repeatability, permutation sensitivity, and caption-data readiness.

Enhancements:
- Document a synthetic LRPO reward null diagnostic and its limitations without claiming an implementation reproduction or benchmark impact.
- Record UCA/VERA cross-split overlap, annotation limitations, metadata hashes, and a rejected category-imbalanced pilot manifest.
- Establish a no-go decision for the current proposal and define evidence, supervision, and mechanism requirements for any future reopening.

Documentation:
- Add research decision records, feasibility report, temporal pilot protocol, and reproducibility documentation.

Tests:
- Add deterministic audits for metadata splits, UCA crosswalks, temporal reward calculations, and pilot-result analysis.

title: Firearm A/G/AG study: localization and its effect on VERA's anomaly judgments
body:
## Summary

This is the study in `studies/firearm/HANDOFF.md`, run on the full VISILAB firearm-action dataset with frozen InternVL2-8B. It asks:

1. What anomaly judgments does unchanged VERA produce?
2. Can the frozen backbone localize firearms against the dataset's boxes?
3. Does requesting localization in the same answer change the judgments?

The run covers 398 videos, 6,375 windows and three conditions on identical eight-frame inputs: A (VERA unchanged), G (grounding only) and AG (VERA plus a grounding request). All 19,125 units completed in one session on one RTX 6000 Ada, with no failures.

**Findings** (from `studies/firearm/results/firearm_a_g_ag_v1/numbers.json`):

- **A** labels 76.3 % of windows anomalous: Handgun 80.4 %, Machine_Gun 87.9 %, No_Gun 57.2 %. The categories are not anomaly labels, so these are not accuracies.
- **Localization:** with VERA's packing of eight frames into one image block, the backbone does not localize.
  - G answered `[]` on 50,804 of 51,000 slots.
  - Every box written was whole-image.
  - Recall against 23,841 annotated firearms is 0 at IoU 0.50 and 0.75, for G and AG alike.
- **AG − A** = −3.8 pp (95 % CI −5.2 to −2.3, video-cluster bootstrap) on 6,370 paired windows.
  - The drop is largest on No_Gun.
  - Refined scores agree: −0.027 per video (−0.039 to −0.014).
  - AG almost never localized, so this is the effect of a bundled prompt change, not of localization.

The study is exploratory: the G/AG prompt format was fixed after a bounded pilot (`PROMPT_LOG.md`).

## What's in this branch

- **Data:** inventory and staging (`vera_runner/firearm_data.py`) and the annotation audit (`firearm_annotations.py`, `AUDIT.md`, `annotation_policy.json`).
- **Prompts and parsers:** A/G/AG prompts (`vera_runner/conditions.py`, `studies/firearm/prompts/`, locked by sha256); strict parsers (`vera_runner/slots.py`).
- **Backend:** `InternVL2.predict(..., question=None)`. With the default, A's call is unchanged: `run_vera.py` and study A gave byte-identical output on 12 pilot windows in 3 runs.
- **Runner:** resumable with a unit ledger (`vera_runner/study.py`, `ledger.py`, `run_firearm_study.py`).
- **Features and refinement:** LAVAD-procedure ImageBind features (`imagebind_features.py`, `FEATURES_VALIDATION.md`) and offline refinement.
- **Metrics:** localization matching (`localization.py`).
- **Analysis:** T1–T11 and P1–P9 (`studies/firearm/analysis/`); the LaTeX report (`studies/firearm/report/`).
- **Results:** `studies/firearm/results/firearm_a_g_ag_v1/` holds every table as CSV, the numbers, the qualitative cases, `report.pdf` (26 pages) and `report_source.zip`; `RESULTS.md` summarises them.
- **Review:** pre-run independent review and its resolutions (`REVIEW.md`; an AI review, not a human signature).

## Reproduce

Commands are in `studies/firearm/README.md`: prepare, audit, convert, validate, pilot, the full run, reconcile, features-check, features, refine, analyze, report build. The exact configuration is `studies/firearm/experiment_A_G_AG.annotated.yaml`. The run's immutable `spec.json` and every record stay on Oz.

## Notes for review

- **Draft, not for merge yet.** `feature/configurable-runner` and `feature/vera-lab` are kept identical, so a merge should move both.
- `experiment/firearm-vera-training1` (Training 1, a separate session and PR) cherry-picks this branch's data commits and byte-copies `ledger.py`, so the two branches add the same files.
- **This repo is public.** `report.pdf` shows frames from the VISILAB dataset: faces blurred by its authors; CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo and CC BY-NC 3.0 on Mendeley; attributed in the report.
- **Tests:** `tests/run_tests.py --suite all` passes: 128 tests, 2 skipped (real model, ImageBind env).

title: Training 1: VERA verbalized learning for firearm categories and actions
body:
## Summary

Training 1 adapts VERA to the VISILAB firearm-action dataset with VERA's own method. InternVL2-8B (rev 6fb9ad69) stays frozen and rewrites its guiding questions (verbalized learning, `training.py`). No boxes are used; boxes are Training 2. Each answer explains the scene through the questions, then names:
- the category (Handgun / Machine_Gun / No_Gun);
- the action group (6);
- the action code (41).

**Results** (240 train / 62 val / 96 test videos, leak-free split; seed questions score 54.8% on validation and 59.4% on test):

| Run | Val. category | Test category [95% CI] | Test − seed, paired [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faithful VERA, run seed 20261026 | 51.6% | 61.5% [52.0, 70.7] | +2.1 pp [−4.3, +8.6] |
| Faithful VERA, run seed 20261027 | 58.1% | 54.2% [48.0, 60.0] | −5.2 pp [−12.6, +2.1] |
| Faithful VERA, run seed 20261028 | 64.5% | 69.8% [60.4, 78.6] | +10.4 pp [+1.0, +20.4] |
| VERA, fixed, run seed 20261026 | 66.1% | 64.6% [55.3, 74.0] | +5.2 pp [−5.3, +16.2] |
| VERA, fixed, run seed 20261027 | 53.2% | 56.2% [46.7, 66.7] | −3.1 pp [−12.4, +6.1] |
| VERA, fixed, run seed 20261028 | 56.5% | 69.8% [61.0, 79.1] | +10.4 pp [+4.1, +18.1] |
| Question bank | 53.2% | 55.2% [48.9, 61.2] | −4.2 pp [−12.6, +3.9] |
| Bank, random pairs (ablation) | 38.7% | 37.5% [32.0, 43.6] | −21.9 pp [−30.5, −13.5] |
| Bank, no scoring (ablation) | 50.0% | 57.3% [48.5, 65.6] | −2.1 pp [−8.2, +4.2] |

- **Neither variant reliably beats VERA or the neutral seed questions.**
  - The spread across run seeds is about 15 pp for faithful VERA and 14 pp for the fixed variant, as large as any difference between methods.
  - Mean test accuracy is 61.8% for VERA and 63.5% for the fixed variant.
- **The fixed variant won the declared validation comparison (66.1%), but its replications did not repeat it** (53.2% and 56.5% on validation).
- **Random pairs hurt.** Choosing the bank's pairs at random instead of from the learner's confusions is the only run clearly worse than the seed questions.
- **The faithful run's main error is handguns called No_Gun** (32 of 37 with the seed questions, 23 of 37 with the learned questions).
- **Determinism:** the seed questions gave identical test answers in all nine runs.
- **Statistics:** intervals resample recording groups within category (2,000 draws), with the same draws for every run.

**Reports on Oz:**
- `training1/report_combined/main.pdf`: all runs, 18 pages.
- `training1/analysis/report/main.pdf`: the faithful run only.

Model time across the nine runs came to about 32.5 GPU hours (from the run logs), on GPUs 5, 6 and 7.

## What's in the branch

- **Data:** cherry-picked from `study/firearm-a-g-ag`: inventory and staging, box validation, annotation audit, backend telemetry, the append-only ledger.
- **Design, codebook and prompts:**
  - `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-firearm-vera-training1-design.md`;
  - `studies/firearm_training/codebook.py`, which writes the codebook, VERA's prompts adapted to 3 categories, 6 groups and 41 codes, and the neutral seed questions.
- **Split:** `studies/firearm_training/prepare.py` writes 240/62/96 videos. No recording group spans two splits, and every code is in every split.
- **Faithful trainer:** `vera_runner/verbalized.py`. Learner `batch_chat` on 2 videos × 8 frames, optimizer `chat` on 16 frames, VERA's five-line question update, validation every 100 batches, 10 epochs, greedy decoding, 1,024 tokens. A test executes VERA's own `forward` and `training_step` on a fake model to check faithfulness. The run is resumable, and `spec.json` is immutable and hash-checked.
- **Declared variants:** `vera_runner/verbalized_variants.py`, with a literature note in `studies/firearm_training/LITERATURE.md`.
  - **VERA, fixed:** balanced batches, OPRO-style score history, accept-if-not-worse on a fixed check set, no "describe" questions.
  - **Confusion-pair yes/no question bank:** adapted from ESCHER and FuDD, with random-pair and no-scoring ablations.
- **Analysis and report:**
  - `studies/firearm_training/analysis/run.py`: tables S1–S10 and figures F1–F4.
  - `analysis/compare.py`: cross-run tables C1–C4, figures G1–G3, and `decide` for the depth runs.
  - `report/`: the LaTeX sources, with an optional section on variants and replications.
- **Jobs:** `studies/firearm_training/jobs/`: smoke, train, the GPU chains and the depth runs.
- **CLI:** `run_firearm_training.py` with `prepare`, `train`, `test`, `check-spec`, `analyze`, `compare` and `decide`.

## Overnight runs

GPUs 6 and 7 run the overnight plan, declared in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-firearm-training1-variants-plan.md` before any result:
- faithful replications with run seeds 20261027 and 20261028;
- the fixed variant;
- the question bank and its two ablations;
- then the depth runs on the validation winner.

Changes after launch, before any variant result:
- the smoke runs were fixed;
- the fixed optimizer was kept inside InternVL2-8B's 8,192-token context: 3 frames per video, and history trimmed to fit.

You approved a third GPU (GPU 5) for the winner's second replication. Every change is recorded in the plan doc.

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python tests/run_tests.py --suite firearm`: 36 tests pass, including faithfulness to VERA's `training.py`, split leakage, both variants on a fake model, the comparison and the depth decision.
- [x] Smoke on Oz (2 steps, 4 validation and 4 test videos), then the full faithful run (exit 0, tested).
- [x] Report built on Oz with pdflatex and bibtex: 12 pages, no undefined references or `??` values, no overfull boxes.
- [x] All nine runs finished (exit 0, tested); `compare` and the combined report built: 18 pages, no undefined references, no overfull boxes.

title: Add VERA Lab: live run view, model boxes, warm model, Mac MPS and Oz runs
body:
VERA's original score generator saves a 0/1 result for each sampled window. It drops the generated prose and never cites which of the eight images supports a claim. VERA Lab is a localhost page over the configurable runner. It runs one window, or one video through preprocessing, all-window inference, refinement or evaluation. It then shows the eight images the model saw, the text it wrote, and every file each stage saved.

The first commit added the lab. The follow-up commits finish the work that was still open, address the automated review, record real-model acceptance on CUDA and on a Mac, and show where the model runs and what it uses.

## What the follow-up commits change

**Runner** (`vera_runner/`, `run_vera.py`)
- `model.dtype: auto` follows the resolved device: CUDA BF16, MPS FP16, CPU FP32. `model_identity.json` records the device and precision actually used.
- With `local_files_only: true`, a Hub ID now resolves to an already-cached snapshot of the configured revision. Before, it was rejected unless the path was a directory.
- `model.revision: null` uses the Hub default branch; the loaded commit is recorded as `resolved_commit`.
- `model.flash_attention: auto` turns FlashAttention on for CUDA when flash-attn is installed, as upstream VERA ran.
- `prepare_environment()` sets `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK` and the repository `HF_HOME` default for both the runner and the lab's window process.
- `configure(cfg)` lets a loaded backend take a new prompt and generation settings without reloading weights.
- The real-model test now creates its ignored log folder. On a fresh checkout it used to crash after a successful model run.

**Lab server** (`tools/demo_server.py`, `tools/window_probe.py`)
- One-window runs go to a persistent process (`window_probe.py --serve`) that keeps the model loaded. Changing checkpoint, device, precision or download starts a new one. Full-video runs stop it first. It exits after 15 idle minutes.
- `auto` device now gets MPS CPU fallback. The pinned revision applies only to `OpenGVLab/InternVL2-8B` and local copies. Non-finite start times are rejected in the probe itself. Die candidates are sorted, so a seeded pick is reproducible.
- `GET /api/windows` returns each window's label, frames and response, without token IDs, for the full-video strip.
- `GET /api/usage` (`tools/usage.py`) reports the server's host, the process holding the model, and read-only GPU and process usage: `nvidia-smi` on CUDA; `ioreg` and `top` on a Mac.
- Both subprocess launches use fixed argument lists without a shell. User input reaches them only through the config file or the JSON request on stdin; the lines are annotated for opengrep.

**Lab page** (`tools/web/`)
- The run page opens on a two-lane pipeline: what InternVL2 sees per window, and the whole-video stages. It highlights the stages the selected run includes, and each stage jumps to the knob that changes it.
- Video drop, a ⚄ "I'm feeling lucky" die, and the knobs grouped beside it. Precision defaults to "Auto for device".
- After a full-video run, a strip shows every window's label. Selecting one shows its eight inputs and its response.
- A usage panel under the run status shows which machine runs the model (through the tunnel that is Oz, not the Mac), GPU busy %, GPU memory, and the model process's CPU and memory.
- **↺ Reset to VERA defaults** restores every knob and clears the video. Defaults are VERA's original settings: pinned InternVL2-8B, released questions, BF16 + FlashAttention on CUDA, greedy decoding with 1024 new tokens. The lab previously capped output at 512 tokens with FlashAttention off.
- Score plots have axes. The theme follows the system until the viewer picks one. Navigation is the same on every page.
- Late die or upload replies no longer overwrite a newer choice, and a dropped status request is retried instead of abandoning the run.

**Boxes, live view, exact prompt** (after the user's go; the WI-02 InternVL3.5 integration is a separate branch and PR)
- `vera_runner/grounding.py` follows grounding pilot WI-01. A window labelled 1 gets a naming follow-up in the same conversation, then one model-card grounding call per image. Boxes are read from the decode that keeps `<ref>`/`<box>`, on a 0–1000 grid of the 448 px input. A first box covering ≥ 95 % of the image is `full_frame` ("not a location"), never a hit. Runner config `boxes.mode` is `off` by default; the lab turns it on.
- Live record: `timeline.jsonl` gets every step (window sampled, text while generated, label, naming, each box, refinement, metrics); `model_input.txt` holds the exact language-model input.
- Page:
  - simple and advanced views;
  - the stage running now is outlined with its latest real value;
  - an "Exact prompt" panel, rendered by the runner's `prompt()`, plus the full model input (template and system message);
  - a player that follows live or replays windows in time order: 8 inputs, streaming text, label, box overlays with tagged output, final frame-score cursor, event log;
  - manual boxes on any frames you pick.
- Measured: streaming adds about 0.03 s per window and leaves text unchanged (25/25 identical). A slowdown found while testing is fixed: the runner reopened `model_progress.jsonl` every forward pass, which doubled time per window on Oz's NFS home (4.35 s → 2.2 s after the fix).

**Docs**: `DEMO.md` (Mac and Oz setup, knobs, warm model, acceptance), `RUNNER.md` (removed stale Mac-only notes; dtype, revision and cache behaviour), `tests/README.md`, `tests/reports/`.

## Task checklist

| Task (source) | Status | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive explainer of how InternVL2 takes input, matched to code | Done | `/how-it-works`, plus the pipeline on `/` |
| Run the real model from the page on Mac MPS, RTX 6000 Ada or CPU | Done; MPS and CUDA verified | Device and precision knobs; see Validation |
| Explain scene refinement → smoothing → frame expansion → timeline | Done | `/scores`, and each stage's arrays in the stage viewer |
| Lab is a separate tool with a clean design | Done | `tools/` only; runner scripts unchanged except the items above |
| Make it efficient | Done: warm model | Two consecutive windows: 31.0 s → 4.6 s (Oz), 35.3 s → 11.1 s (Mac) |
| Study guide removed; real problem stated next to "Run one window" | Done | Callout under the run button |
| Drop a video; picture of the model and knobs; die + "I'm feeling lucky", tested | Done | `/`; `tests/demo/test_demo_server.py` die tests |
| Light/dark, cleaner colours, interactive first, separate linked pages | Done | Theme button; four pages in the nav |
| Fix `No module named 'cv2'` on the Mac | Done | `.venv` from `requirements-runner.txt`; preflight names missing modules |
| Save every stage of a run to one scratch folder, cleared per run, clear names | Done | `demo_runs/current/`, `stage_manifest.json` (`00_request` … `08_diagnostics`) |
| Finish the full-video acceptance run and check the stage viewer | Done | Validation below; Oz evidence folder |
| Sync Oz to the PR and restart its lab server | Done | Oz `~/vera_research/setup/source/VERA-lab` on this branch |
| Address the open Sourcery review threads | Done | Each thread has a reply naming the fix |
| Update stale acceptance docs on the runner branch | Done | `tests/reports/ONE_WINDOW_ACCEPTANCE.md` |
| Show which machine runs the model and its usage | Done | Usage panel under the run status; `DEMO.md` "Where it runs" |
| Default to VERA's original config; reset button | Done | ↺ Reset; reproduces experiment01 exactly (below) |
| Bounding boxes from the model, only for anomalous windows; others on request | Done | Run a window labelled 1, or tick "Pick frames to box" |
| Live, transparent timelapse of what the model does; exact prompts | Done | "Exact prompt" panel; player and event log under the run |

## Validation

- `tests/run_tests.py --suite all`: 52 discovered, 51 passed, 1 skipped (the opt-in real-model test), on the Mac (`.venv`, Python 3.11) and on Oz. The `lab` suite (27 tests) and the runner's box parser and boxes pipeline tests drives the HTTP API and the real warm process with the mock backend.
- `tests/run_tests.py --suite real-model`: passed on Oz (RTX 6000 Ada, CUDA BF16; 4.9 s generation, label 0) and on an M3 Max Mac (MPS FP16; 16.5 s generation, label 0). Both had the same 2487 input tokens.
- Full video on Oz with VERA's original settings (now the lab default): all 162 responses word for word identical to experiment01, same 13 alert windows, frame ROC-AUC 0.9949414519906323, in 7.7 minutes. With the lab's earlier settings (no FlashAttention, 512 tokens) one window differed (anchor 496) and the run took 17 minutes. A second full run on the final code gave the same 162 labels, AUC and AP (17.4 minutes).
- Browser: run page at 1280 px and 375 px (no horizontal scroll), both themes, die, stage highlighting, click-to-knob, stage viewer and plots on the finished Oz run. Usage panel checked on the Mac with the model loaded: 34 GB GPU-allocated unified memory, 30 GB process footprint. On Oz the RTX 6000 Ada showed 53 % busy with 22 GB held by a full-video run.
- Boxes on Oz, whole RoadAccidents127 through the page: experiment01's 13 alert windows were boxed (104 calls: 57 box, 47 whole image), with labels and AUC unchanged. The run took 10.4 minutes. Phrases included "Train collision with truck".
- Boxes on the Mac (MPS), window at 74 s: the model named "Red truck and train crossing at the same time" and boxed the truck in images 1–4, with whole-image replies on 5, 6 and 8, about 2 s per call. Manual boxes for "the train" on two picked images worked and are saved separately.
- `node --check` on all lab scripts.

## Try it

```bash
uv venv --seed --python 3.11 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-runner.txt
.venv/bin/python tests/run_tests.py --suite all
.venv/bin/python tools/demo_server.py --port 8765 --video-dir <videos> --model-path <InternVL2-8B checkpoint>
```

Oz commands and the SSH tunnel are in `DEMO.md`.

title: Report full experiment03B results with preserved records and R1 integrity audit
body:
The full experiment03B run is complete. Its original primary result is **+15.166 percentage points [95% CI 9.860, 20.600]**: blur-ranked top-two frames remove original VERA alerts under grey replacement more often than the exact mean over all 28 grey pairs (199 alert windows, 138 videos). This is perturbation-ranking utility, not detection improvement or proof of semantic faithfulness.

Stack 5 of 5; base remains `research/experiment03A-protocol` (#4). Draft for human review; no merge requested.

## Full run and preserved evidence

- Frozen protocol v1.1; 290 UCF videos, 433 available inputs; no new inference in this amendment.
- Commit includes previously untracked full-run raw requests, cache, frozen metadata, derived values, original tables, ledger and failed validator artifact.
- Original validation remains **16 passed / 4 failed**. No original score, label, ranking, estimate or validation artifact was edited.
- All 36 local source files are covered by before/after SHA256 preservation checks. The portable manifest covers 31 record files; the ignored runtime lock and four dataset-derived example files remain local, with hashes retained.

## Explicit post-data integrity amendment R1

R1 reruns the original validator and reconciles only four contract errors; the remaining sixteen checks are unchanged. **R1: 20 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.** It is a disclosed reconciliation with knowledge of the failures, not a fresh blinded review.

1. Numerical check now verifies the engine's pre-existing half-BF16-step + 0.001 tolerance. All 45 exact-rounding mismatches remain reported (max half-step excess 0.0001716614); no claim of exact rounding.
2. Slot-hash check recomputes the legacy flag instead of demanding true even for no-op transforms.
3. Only hash-verified all-black source frames unchanged by blur are accepted as no-ops. Unmasked changes, unexplained no-ops and inconsistent replacements fail.
4. Shared sequence keys require equal source/frame/transform/tensor identity, not equal video names. Archived Normal_Videos_936 and 937 were independently SHA256-verified as identical.

A separately reported source-deduplicated sensitivity leaves the primary estimate unchanged. Secondary population falls from 288 video IDs to 287 sources; numeric margin changes 0.355630→0.355919 nats. Other deduplicated metrics and prefixes are included.

## Verification and report

- Original independent-validator tests: **37 passed**.
- R1 corruption regressions: **11 passed**.
- Workflow: **16 substantive local checks passed**, plus the actual pixel-path check **passed separately on Oz**. The legacy local harness printed 17/17 while reporting that pixel check skipped; this is disclosed.
- Initial workflow failures from a missing pinned source dependency are preserved; restoring the documented worktree fixed the environment without workflow-code edits.
- `report_r1/main.tex` compiles successfully; tables and figures are generated from stored JSON/CSV, with a result-integrity gate.

Start review at `experiments/experiment03B/R1_AMENDMENT.md`, then `audits/full_v1_r1/validation_r1.json`, `duplicate_sensitivity.json`, and `report_r1/main.tex`. The original frozen run and failed validator remain available side by side. Registry status is corrected, with earlier snapshots retained as historical.

No subsequent question-learning experiment is part of this PR.

body:

`research/validated-baseline`.

[`a4bb5618`](https://github.com/shridpant/VERA/commit/a4bb56184de986f50b1ffb9b9535a9f60b3bbc46) is a repository-integration commit. No experiment was
run, and no historical record, config or manifest changed.

- **Erratum E1** (`experiments/experiment02/ERRATA.md`). run_002's scoring contract and report say that S_hi
  changes below one bf16 step "cannot change" the deployed output. That is wrong.

    changed the VERA source (`008ed401` today).
